castgate.name: Castgate
castgate.blurb: Encased within a dome that holds the winter at bay, Castgate's picturesque beauty was earned through legendary battles against a goddess and an undead horde. Though its streets bustle with prosperity from gems and ships, the common folk work in the shadow of the very magic that shelters them.
castgate.selectorDescription: A prosperous dome-city that endures winter under old magic.

detailSections.heading: Context

Its walls are decorated with trophies from Sub Rosa’s adventures, making it a symbol of the town’s enduring resilience.

IceBeach.name: IceBeach
IceBeach.blurb: A detailed view of the Icebeach region, a northern arctic frontier of auroras, survival towns, glacier ruins, and post-winter scars.
IceBeach.selectorDescription: A frozen northern frontier of auroras, survival towns, glacier ruins, and post-winter scars.

pointsOfInterest.name: Castgate
pointsOfInterest.description: Castgate is a paradox in the north: a humid, flower-scented town beneath a magical dome while salt, ice, wind, mines, and political ambition press against the barrier outside.
pointsOfInterest.summary: Icebeach's sheltered trade hub, warmed by the rebuilt Firmament and divided between old survivors and wealthy newcomers.

properties.Leadership: Tolin Stillgrove shaped the reconstruction era

detailSections.heading: The Firmament
detailSections.body: The dome was first built by Averios Calytheron, shattered during Morena's assault in the Eternal Winter, and rebuilt after the thaw. Inside, it mimics a clear blue sky and turns Castgate into a tropical-seeming refuge against the polar night.

detailSections.heading: Tension
detailSections.body: The comfort of the dome has become a social fault line. Locals remember survival, Sub Rosa, and old losses, while the Thawed, southern merchants, Athenaeum agents, and wealthy visitors increasingly treat the town as opportunity.

detailSections.heading: Notable places
detailSections.body: The Frozen Rose anchors adventuring and Sub Rosa memory; Bleak's Stand memorializes the dead; the Shrine of Hestia, Frostviel, the Crystal Needle, the Groves of Hope's Rebirth, and the docks all give the town more than a single civic center.

pointsOfInterest.name: Flamore
pointsOfInterest.description: Flamore's School of Experimental Wizardry began as a remote magical redoubt and later became a school, but its turn toward forbidden research under the mountains ended in catastrophe.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A ruined mountain school whose experiments turned from celestial study toward forbidden glacier secrets.

properties.Founded: Castle around 10 BEC; school around 15 BEC

detailSections.heading: History
detailSections.body: The Flamore family built the castle as a private redoubt before Gilded Nations backing formalized it as a school. It originally studied the heavens under Nyx, then shifted toward darker research after a strange timeline-crossing event.

detailSections.heading: The incident
detailSections.body: Exploration beneath the castle uncovered vile tombs, glacier-connected cave systems, and an artifact called the orbit of subnecromancy. Containment failed, zombifying the people inside the wards.

detailSections.heading: Current status
detailSections.body: The ruins remain a warning against academic arrogance, glacier-delving, and treating cosmic horror as a research opportunity.

pointsOfInterest.name: Fractured Point
pointsOfInterest.description: Fractured Point perches above rocky shores where stained-glass lanterns fight the wind and a castle beacon watches the icefield plains.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A walled crag town, lighthouse, trade stop, and first arrival point for many visitors to Icebeach.

properties.Defenses: Walls, gates closed at sundown, castle beacon

detailSections.heading: At a glance
detailSections.body: The town can look festive from a distance, with colored lanterns twisting over narrow streets, but the wind has worn away much of its welcome.

detailSections.heading: Local mood
detailSections.body: Common folk carry the suffering of winter, while traders and the wealthy maintain cheer and opportunity. The settlement is practical, suspicious, and strict about closing its gates at sundown.

pointsOfInterest.name: Gernerum
pointsOfInterest.description: Gernerum is gone, leaving ruins, ash, and stories of a settlement that once shaped Icebeach before disaster consumed it.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A destroyed town remembered for its famous Icebeach figures and its fiery end after a mechanical dragon battle.

detailSections.heading: Memory
detailSections.body: The guide remembers Gernerum as the childhood home or early refuge of figures tied to Icebeach history, including Thorn and Sylva Frostglade.

detailSections.heading: Rumor
detailSections.body: Its only survivor is said to be the vile hag of the north, leaving the ruin with more dread than closure.

pointsOfInterest.name: Houlen Top
pointsOfInterest.description: Marked here as Houlen Top and described in the guide as Howlentop, this fertile valley feeds the north while keeping outsiders at the edge of town.
pointsOfInterest.summary: The southern agricultural anomaly of Icebeach, where unwalled farmsteads produce grains and massive root vegetables.

properties.Defenses: Unwalled; locals trust the valley more than stone

detailSections.heading: People
detailSections.body: The residents are physically imposing, guarded, and communal. They work with synchronized efficiency and rarely let strangers past the Border Market.

detailSections.heading: Local oddities
detailSections.body: Full-moon curfews, refusal to handle silver, and the disappearance of predators or bandits make the town feel less undefended than it first appears.

pointsOfInterest.name: Icemoor
pointsOfInterest.description: Icemoor is marked as a town on southern maps, but most cabins stand empty after families fled the glacier during the Eternal Winter.
pointsOfInterest.summary: An almost-abandoned watchtower settlement facing the Winrich Glacier and its fortress.

properties.Residents: The Old Guard, also called Custodians of the View

detailSections.heading: The Watchers
detailSections.body: A skeleton crew of elderly holdouts maintains the tower and watches for movement from the glacier. They believe the silence is a trick and keep magical warning devices ready, though who receives those alerts is contested.

detailSections.heading: Last stop
detailSections.body: For adventurers, Icemoor is the final warm meal before the white wastes. The Watchers record names in a ledger and expect most travelers never to return.

pointsOfInterest.name: Little Rock Mentle Asylam
pointsOfInterest.description: Little Rock Mental Asylum is a remote containment institution where stone, sea, wards, and despair are all part of the security design.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A grim Gilded Nations asylum for criminals and dangerous minds deemed too risky for ordinary prisons.

properties.Security: Physical walls, wards, psychic dampening, guards and constructs

detailSections.heading: Containment
detailSections.body: The asylum is described as the final destination for criminals, rogue mages, masterminds, killers, and political threats too dangerous to release or execute.

detailSections.heading: Reputation
detailSections.body: Escape is treated as functionally impossible, and the place is said to leave no one unchanged even if they survive long enough to leave.

pointsOfInterest.name: Morana's Fang
pointsOfInterest.description: Morana's Fang is a brutal pilgrimage mountain where the veil to divine and spirit realms thins near the Stillness Summit.
pointsOfInterest.summary: The tallest peak in the world, sacred to the Goddess of Winter and guarded by mysterious Icewind Sentinels.

detailSections.heading: The climb
detailSections.body: The route crosses ice cliffs, wind-scoured ridges, deep crevasses, and the hunting grounds of cold-born monsters. The mountain tests endurance, resolve, and spirit rather than offering ordinary instruction.

detailSections.heading: Sacred danger
detailSections.body: Legends say the summit once allowed direct communion with gods or spirits. Now it offers only cryptic visions, whispers on the wind, or encounters with servants of powers that still listen from the cold.

pointsOfInterest.name: Mt. Solaria
pointsOfInterest.description: Mt. Solaria is a mountain of contradictions, with warmth venting through the cold and legends of an ancient wyrm beneath the gray sky.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A geothermal mountain of steam vents, salmon runs, failed mines, old tombs, and dragon rumors.

properties.Features: Steam vents, caldera, salmon streams, mines, tombs
properties.Rumor: Dragon lair or slumbering wyrm breath

detailSections.heading: Geothermal lure
detailSections.body: Steam vents and sudden thaws draw desperate settlers, fishers, and scholars despite avalanches, predators, and the fear that the dragon may stir.

detailSections.heading: Old scars
detailSections.body: The slopes hold abandoned mines and ancient tomb facades, with rumors of cave-ins, territorial beasts, dragon cults, giant-kin remains, and draugr guarding mountain secrets.

pointsOfInterest.name: Ottiker
pointsOfInterest.description: The town marked here as Ottiker is described in the guide as Niror or Ottiken, a frost-wine settlement caught between immigrant ambition and a bitter druidic feud.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A wine settlement on Sleetmond Lake, called Niror by locals and Ottiken by newer immigrants.

detailSections.heading: Identity
detailSections.body: Astrousian and Last Elven State immigrants have reshaped the town, creating a visible clash between older local identity and new architecture, labor, and commerce.

detailSections.heading: Wine conflict
detailSections.body: Niror Red has become valuable after the thaw, but shipments spike or fail when the feud with druids interferes. The injured Wyrm-Speaker governs through loyalists and a growing mercenary guard.

pointsOfInterest.name: Quilt
pointsOfInterest.description: Quilt is a dockside maker-town whose fish farms and heavy Icesheep quilts depend on the Foaming Burrow keeping local waters alive.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A tiny Foaming Loch town of fish farming, dyed wool, and survival textiles warmed by nearby geothermal vents.

properties.Industries: Aquaculture, dyed wool, quilts and tapestries

detailSections.heading: The artisan economy
detailSections.body: Quilt exports heavy, colorful textiles woven from Icesheep wool. In the south, genuine Quilt tapestry has become a status symbol as much as survival gear.

detailSections.heading: Geothermal dependence
detailSections.body: The town thrived through the Eternal Winter because nearby warm vents kept the waters usable, making the Burrow both a resource and something locals protect fiercely.

pointsOfInterest.name: Shiverwallow
pointsOfInterest.description: Shiverwallow is a hard-working harbor of palisades, breakwaters, fish, smoke, and people shaped by years of frozen-sea survival.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A fortified fishing town at the Chillfolk River, now operating its recovered fleet and winter ice camps.

detailSections.heading: Fleet reborn
detailSections.body: During the Eternal Winter the harbor froze solid, trapping ships and forcing camps onto the ice. Nine years later, the fleet is free again and the harbor is a forest of masts, nets, crews, and salted catch.

detailSections.heading: Ice Walkers
detailSections.body: When winter sea ice returns, part of the population still migrates onto the floes to hunt seals and ice-whales, a tradition admired and feared even by other locals.

pointsOfInterest.name: Sleetmond
pointsOfInterest.description: Sleetmond is a small town on Sleetmond Lake where druids and rangers tend the Hope Tree, sugar maple orchards, fish, and unusually warm Icesheep wool.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A druidic lakeside settlement of sugar maples, fish, Icesheep, and the Hope Tree.

detailSections.heading: Druidic practice
detailSections.body: The town is notable for druidic traditions centered on the Hope Tree. Its people and practices are strange enough that many outsiders and even some natives distrust them.

detailSections.heading: Survival economy
detailSections.body: Sugar maples, lake fish, and Icebeach sheep make Sleetmond more self-sufficient than many northern settlements.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Foaming Burrow
pointsOfInterest.description: The Foaming Burrow is not one cave but a network of steam vents, hot springs, and heated tunnels beneath a snow-free patch of ground.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A geothermal cave network southeast of Quilt that feeds the Foaming Loch and Foaming Runs.

properties.Feature: Steam vents, hot springs, heated tunnels

detailSections.heading: Ecology
detailSections.body: Fire-resistant creatures, salamanders, magmin, druids, and elemental guardians are all plausible inhabitants of its hot chambers.

detailSections.heading: Local tie
detailSections.body: Its heat keeps downstream waters from freezing and even supplies the Firenewt tea pets used by the Fireside Newt and Chai en' Steep Inn.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Hope Tree
pointsOfInterest.description: The Hope Tree rises impossibly in the frozen north, radiating warmth, safety, and restorative magic where Morana's cold should rule.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A warm, green-gold miracle tree that anchors Sleetmond and resists Morana's winter.

detailSections.heading: Sacred theories
detailSections.body: Most locals treat it as a blessing of Hestia, though other stories name Pythia, Bethtox, or an old divine confrontation with Morana as the reason the cold fails here.

detailSections.heading: Restorative power
detailSections.body: Its leaves remain green and gold and can be brewed into healing teas, making the tree a symbol of community and a resource no sane local would willingly harm.

pointsOfInterest.name: Thrawbreak
pointsOfInterest.description: Thrawbreak began as a mountaineer camp below the Auruan mountains and now survives between failed fortifications, a frozen harbor, and one known pass.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A remote mountain hamlet of ruined defenses, frozen docks, hard beer, and cut-off resentment.

detailSections.heading: Isolation
detailSections.body: With the ferry from Whitedrift shut down, Thrawbreak is cut off by mountains, ice, and snow. Its people believe the rest of the world abandoned them.

detailSections.heading: Local trouble
detailSections.body: Recent mysterious break-ins and the speaker's drunken night patrols add paranoia to a town already surviving on stubbornness and a tavern that never seems to run dry.

pointsOfInterest.name: Whitedrift
pointsOfInterest.description: Whitedrift clings to the mouth of the Curse Run, fed by Winrich Glacier melt, and carries the instability of people stationed too close to horror for too long.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A rocky Curse Run settlement watching the glacier, the fortress, and the asylum nearby.

detailSections.heading: Population
detailSections.body: Some residents are assigned to keep watch on the glacier and fortress, while others are said to be escapees or castoffs from the asylum.

detailSections.heading: Atmosphere
detailSections.body: The settlement feels unstable by design: a cold rock town where glacial water, institutional shadow, and paranoia all meet.

pointsOfInterest.name: Winrich Fortress
pointsOfInterest.description: Winrich Fortress drinks light from the glacier wind and remains a decaying monument to ancient necromancy, traps, undead, and deliberate misdirection.
pointsOfInterest.summary: The black-stone ruin of Winrich, remembered as perhaps the first mortal lich.

properties.Phenomenon: Sickly green-blue glow on darkest nights

detailSections.heading: Purpose
detailSections.body: Legends claim the fortress stood over a dark confluence called the soul well, but some scholars think Winrich built it as a decoy to hide his true phylactery and treasures elsewhere.

detailSections.heading: Current danger
detailSections.body: The ruin is shunned for lesser undead, undetonated traps, psychic residue, and periodic spectral light similar to the glow reported inside Winrich Glacier.

pointsOfInterest.name: Wynwood Peak
pointsOfInterest.description: Wynwood Peak is less imposing in height than other mountains but feared for unnatural timber, difficult slopes, and the lingering evil of a ruined wizard tower.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A smaller but treacherous peak covered in iron-hard woods and haunted by dragon-mound stories.

properties.Rumor: Dragon mound or ancient wyrm burial

detailSections.heading: Wynwood timber
detailSections.body: The trees are said to resist axe and saw, with roots that anchor into stone and wood that may carry protective magic from an ancient dragon burial.

detailSections.heading: The tower
detailSections.body: A wizard drawn by the peak's rumored energies went mad and evil here. Though defeated, the tower remains feared for haunting and a hostile spirit bound to the mountain.

regions.name: Ded Moros Forest
regions.description: Ded Moros Forest is not dead so much as unnaturally preserved, with gray stone trees, fossilized leaves, sharp branches, and roots that turn the forest floor into a maze.
regions.summary: A grim woodland of petrified trees, old curse stories, and creatures adapted to stone-like forest remains.

detailSections.heading: Threats
detailSections.body: The guide ties its condition to an ancient curse or magical catastrophe, perhaps connected to Winrich. Stone-skinned predators, sorrowful spirits, and other adapted creatures may lurk in its silence.

regions.name: Frostmaple Grove
regions.description: Frostmaple Grove is believed to be the primordial source of Sleetmond's sugar maple orchards, with gold-touched leaves and thick old bark even in deep winter.
regions.summary: An ancient wild heartwood of unnaturally large frostmaples, sweet air, and slumbering treant guardians.

detailSections.heading: Lore
detailSections.body: Treants are said to guard the grove, and sap drawn from its oldest trees may have restorative or life-extending properties beyond ordinary food.

regions.name: Foaming Loch
regions.description: The Foaming Loch lies in a basin of snow and dark stone, its surface broken by mist, mineral foam, and patches of open water warmed from below. Heat flowing from the Foaming Burrow keeps the lake alive through the northern winter, supporting Quilt's fish farms before the turbulent water continues into the Foaming Runs.
regions.summary: A geothermal lake whose warm, restless waters sustain Quilt and feed the Foaming Runs even through IceBeach's deepest cold.

regions.name: Sleetmond Lake
regions.description: Sleetmond Lake stretches beneath the northern sky between the druidic settlement of Sleetmond and the vineyards of Ottiker. Its cold waters provide fish for nearby communities, while sugar maples, grazing Icesheep, and the grapes used for Niror Red flourish along its shores. When the sky is clear, auroras ripple across the lake's broad surface.
regions.summary: A broad northern lake shared by Sleetmond and Ottiker, sustaining fishing, orchards, Icesheep, and the region's prized frost-wine.

regions.name: Starcaller's Grove
regions.description: Starcaller's Grove stands apart from the snow drifts, with clearer skies, brighter stars, vibrant auroras, and moss-covered stones arranged in old patterns.
regions.summary: A bright-sky standing-stone grove where auroras, stars, and divination feel unusually near.

detailSections.heading: Pilgrimage
detailSections.body: Druids, northern wanderers, and seers come seeking enhanced divination, communion with sky spirits, Nyx, or signs of thin places between worlds.

regions.name: The Foaming Runs
regions.description: The Foaming Runs are marked by churning whitewater where icy river flow meets underground heat, producing dangerous steam and foam.
regions.summary: A turbulent river course of rapids, foam, steam, and geothermal vents fed from a cave source.

detailSections.heading: Travel hazard
detailSections.body: The river is especially treacherous near lakes, caves, and vent-fed sections, where hot plumes and violent rapids complicate crossing or navigation.

regions.name: The Frigid Plains
regions.description: The Frigid Plains are featureless and dangerous, with sudden whiteouts that punish poor navigation and expose travelers to the worst open tundra conditions.
regions.summary: A vast wind-scoured tundra of whiteouts, monster hunts, hidden battlefields, and haunted snow.

detailSections.heading: Hidden dangers
detailSections.body: The plains are hunting grounds for massive Ice Tundra Beasts and burrowing monsters like remorhazes. Shifting snow can reveal ancient battlefields and spectral remnants.

regions.name: Winrich Glacier
regions.description: Winrich Glacier dominates Icebeach fear: a frozen mass associated with the first lich, dark ruins, and the sense that silence from the ice is never truly safe.
regions.summary: A sickly green-blue glacier tied to Winrich, old necromancy, and horrors still preserved in the ice.

detailSections.heading: Why it matters
detailSections.body: Icemoor watches it, Whitedrift lives with its meltwater, Flamore delved toward its horrors, and Winrich Fortress still echoes its unnatural glow.

IceBeach.summary: A northern arctic tundra of frozen coasts, hard frontier villages, auroras, and old dangers left behind by the Endless Winter.
IceBeach.description: Icebeach lies far northwest of Fair, where coastal towns cling to frozen beaches and the habitable world gives way to permafrost, glacier, and polar sea. Nine years after the Endless Winter broke, its people remain split between the Frozen, hardened survivors of the long dark, and the Thawed, newcomers drawn by trade, mining, wine, fish, and other opportunities exposed by the melt.

properties.Climate: Arctic tundra, frozen coasts, severe winter darkness
properties.Recent history: Nine years since the Endless Winter ended

detailSections.heading: Environment
detailSections.body: Icebeach is defined by ice sheets on its beaches, brutal cold, blizzards, avalanches, and long seasonal extremes. Summer can bring sleepless midnight sun, while deep winter brings the Long Night, blue-hour twilight, auroras, light pillars, diamond dust, sun dogs, and deceptive sea mirages.

detailSections.heading: Settlements
detailSections.body: Its towns survive through strict necessity rather than shared comfort. Some compete during brief summers, but the settlements maintain a survival pact against the lethal cold, monsters of the north, and the old magical threats still buried in glacier and ruin.

detailSections.heading: Travel
detailSections.body: Travel is a struggle against mountains, tundra, snow, ice, and visibility. Dogsleds, snowshoes, ferries, passes, and local guides can matter more than coin when weather cuts roads apart or the whiteout separates a party.

southern-thalassia.name: Southern Thalassia
southern-thalassia.blurb: Southern Thalassia is a significant maritime region characterized by a series of islands formed and scared by the 'Night of Falling Stars,' an event wherein lunar and asteroidal fragments impacted the region, depositing exotic minerals and creating unique geological formations. This celestial deposition has resulted in altered atmospheric conditions, residual magical energies, and a notable biodiversity influenced by stellar radiation, making the region a focal point for historical study, resource acquisition (particularly rare minerals and energy concentrations), and contested maritime activity, including piracy, with various factions vying for control over these transformed territories.  This map is still under devlopment.
southern-thalassia.selectorDescription: An unfinished maritime map of star-scarred islands and pirate waters.

pointsOfInterest.name: Cavaross
pointsOfInterest.description: Once a simple fishing village, Cavaross was reshaped into the fortified harbor for the Beccin Empire's main fleet.
pointsOfInterest.summary: Once a simple fishing village, Cavaross was reshaped into the fortified harbor for the Beccin Empire's main fleet.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: In the wake of a swift rebellion against its tyrannical governor, the city now breathes a cautious and uncertain air of newfound freedom.

pointsOfInterest.name: Eastwatch
pointsOfInterest.description: Originally founded as a strategic trading post and lookout, this seaside haven hosts a naval academy for the Argentum Compact with the quiet readiness of the Gilded Nation forces stationed there.
pointsOfInterest.summary: Originally founded as a strategic trading post and lookout, this seaside haven hosts a naval academy for the Argentum Compact with the quiet readiness of the Gilded Nation...

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: Orignialy called 'Port Fair Wind,' it was destoryed by Pirate Blackbeard in one of his notorius raids, razing the oringal settlment - a reclusive inventor was able to get word out for help saving the remaining peoples.

pointsOfInterest.name: Fyllns Hold
pointsOfInterest.description: An old coastal town whose very name whispers of a legendary adventurer's hidden riches from a time before the Falling Stars.
pointsOfInterest.summary: An old coastal town whose very name whispers of a legendary adventurer's hidden riches from a time before the Falling Stars.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: While it serves as a simple rest stop for traders today, a persistent undercurrent of treasure hunting ensures the legend never dies.

pointsOfInterest.name: Gales Rest
pointsOfInterest.description: Named for the unnatural calm of its cove, which offers a perfect haven from any storm, this town began as a simple resupply settlement.
pointsOfInterest.summary: Named for the unnatural calm of its cove, which offers a perfect haven from any storm, this town began as a simple resupply settlement.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: Today, it remains a vital sanctuary where even pirates find temporary, if uneasy, anchor.

pointsOfInterest.name: Golden Sands
pointsOfInterest.description: The island's orignal name is now lost to time, and is a private paradise of soft beaches and rich plantations.
pointsOfInterest.summary: The island's orignal name is now lost to time, and is a private paradise of soft beaches and rich plantations.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: It is an exclusive resort where even the field workers move with a leisurely swagger, serving as a sun-drenched playground for the elite of the Athenaeum.

pointsOfInterest.name: Moonshadow Cove
pointsOfInterest.description: Carved into the island in the shape of a perfect crescent, this ancient temple aligns with the moon.
pointsOfInterest.summary: Carved into the island in the shape of a perfect crescent, this ancient temple aligns with the moon.

detailSections.heading: Context

Gelwood.name: Gelwood
Gelwood.blurb: Located on the southern side of the Ardoise Mountains and just off the old Chemin de Ronceval (Ronceval Road), Gelwood is a town defined by resilience. This revived frontier settlement is built upon the moss-covered stone foundations of a much older, forgotten settlement. In the last handful of years, hardy settlers from Rockdrift and Ironstream have begun to reclaim the ruins, building their homes and livelihoods amidst the ghosts of the past. It is now a burgeoning community of farmers, woodcutters, fur traders, and ambitious prospectors, all drawn by persistent tales of gold, platinum, and even diamonds hidden in the nearby mountains.
Gelwood.selectorDescription: A frontier town rebuilt on old stone and drawing settlers and prospectors.

regions.name: Barthan's Traders
regions.description: Run by Barthan Ironhand, a retired dwarven prospector with a kindly smile and hands like worn stone, this shop is the heart of Gelwood's commerce. The air within smells of sawdust, cured leather, and pickling spices. Barthan's stocks everything a settler could need, from sturdy axes and mining equipment to bolts of wool cloth, dried rations, and medicinal herbs. He is a font of local knowledge and is always willing to share a bit of news or a useful rumor with his customers.

regions.name: Edermath Orchard
regions.description: This beautiful orchard is tended by the Edermath family, a quiet half-elven clan who claim their ancestors planted the original trees centuries ago. The orchard miraculously survived the downfall of the previous settlement and was reclaimed from the wild by the family. They cultivate exceptionally crisp, tart apples and produce a famously potent cider that is a favorite at the Sleeping Giant tavern. The grove is known for its serene, almost unnaturally peaceful atmosphere.

regions.name: Shrine To All
regions.description: Rather than a single temple, this sacred space is an open-air collection of small, hand-built shrines nestled within the crumbling stone walls of an ancient ruin. Each alcove is dedicated to a different deity, reflecting the diverse faiths of the settlers who came seeking a new life. Offerings of wildflowers, carved wooden figures, and coins are left by the hopeful. The shrine is quietly maintained by an elderly woman named Lena, who ensures that all gods, great and small, are shown their due respect.

regions.name: Sleeping Giant
regions.description: Named for the massive, dormant mountain peak visible from its front door, this ale house is Gelwood's rowdiest establishment. Run by a boisterous and sharp-witted retired sellsword named Grelka, it is the favored haunt of prospectors, trappers, and traders. The air is thick with pipe smoke, the smell of spilled ale, and the sound of tall tales being spun. The 'Giant's Brew,' a dark and deceptively strong ale, is the tavern's signature drink and the cause of many morning regrets.

regions.name: Smithy
regions.description: The constant, rhythmic clang of a hammer on steel is the heartbeat of Gelwood, emanating from this open-air smithy built into the sturdy foundation of an old watchtower. The smith is a powerfully built and taciturn woman named Brynn. She specializes in crafting and repairing the tools of the trade: sharp axes, durable pickaxes, and reliable shovel heads. While she can mend a sword or forge a helmet, her true passion lies in creating practical, long-lasting tools for the hardworking folk of the town.

regions.name: Stonehill Inn
regions.description: As the only inn in Gelwood, Stonehill provides a much-needed respite for weary travelers and a quieter social hub for the locals. It is run by a warm and welcoming halfling couple, Erion and Miri Stonehill. The rooms are modest but always impeccably clean, and Miri's hearty rabbit stew is renowned along the Ronceval Road. The common room, with its crackling hearth, is a more family-friendly alternative to the Sleeping Giant, offering warm meals and softer conversation.

The-Port-City-of-Stomion.selectorDescription: A hard-edged river-delta port of docks, districts, and imperial pressure.

pointsOfInterest.name: Baths of the Devine Mother
pointsOfInterest.description: An oasis of pristine white marble and verdant greenery amidst the smog of Stomion, the Baths of the Divine Mother are a sanctuary dedicated to Pythia, the Primordial Lifegiver.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A pristine, marble-clad sanctuary and bathhouse dedicated to Pythia, featuring lush gardens and a natural warm spring that serves as a quiet, neutral retreat for the city's elite.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: Fed by the city's only remaining natural spring, the water is naturally warm and famed for its revitalizing properties. The interior is a humidity-filled paradise where exotic flora—blessed by the influence of Veridia—thrives under skylights and soft candlelight, defying the harsh industrial climate outside. A breathtaking statue of Pythia stands at the center of the main pool, her arms outstretched as if offering the waters to the bathers below. Operated by the Lifewardens and a quiet staff of attendants, the facility maintains a strict policy of equality; within these walls, nobles and merchants bathe side-by-side without segregation, weapons, or rank, though the clientele remains largely exclusive due to its location. Silence is heavily encouraged, allowing the sound of trickling water to dominate the air. High Warden Thyleesha currently manages the baths, though she grows increasingly anxious as recent industrial run-off from the neighboring districts threatens to taint the ancient, mysterious source of their holy spring.

pointsOfInterest.name: Beccin Chancery Embasy
pointsOfInterest.description: Constructed within what was once a public park, the Beccin Embassy is a monolithic palace of cold, solid stone that feels utterly alien amidst the weathered architecture of Oldfort.
pointsOfInterest.summary: The imposing stone headquarters of the Vardenheim Directorate, ruled by the clinical and ruthless Overseer Verrick, serving as the true center of Imperial control and secret police operations.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: It serves as the headquarters for the Vardenheim Directorate and the seat of Overseer Intendant Verrick, the 'Hand of the Emperor.' Verrick is a 'Sanitized Tyrant' who views the occupation not as a war, but as a failing factory requiring correction; he wears pristine white gloves to metaphorically and literally keep the filth of the city at bay. The interior is chillingly cold and decorated with imposing propaganda of the Emperor. While the upper floors are a maze of dismissively polite bureaucracy where meetings are nearly impossible to secure, the lower levels house the Directorate's interrogation cells. It is guarded by a specialized detachment of the City Watch, ensuring that Verrick's industrial dismantling of the rebellion proceeds without interruption.

pointsOfInterest.name: Breads and Dregs
pointsOfInterest.description: A chaotic, warm, and wonderfully loud establishment that serves as the beating heart of Northgate's social scene.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A popular bakery-tavern in Northgate offering lodging, strong coffee, and famous 'Road Kits' for travelers, known for its warm atmosphere and century-old sourdough starter.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: Breads and Dregs acts as both a premier bakery and a tavern, catering to weary travelers and locals alike. The air is permanently thick with the comforting scent of yeast and roasting grains, obscuring the smell of the city outside. They are famous for their 'Road Kits'—pre-wrapped ration packs of hardtack, dried meats, and cheese—and a legendary sourdough starter rumored to be over a century old and perhaps slightly sentient. The tavern offers lodging upstairs, and the common room is a dog-friendly haven where local bands play at night and sleepy wagon-drivers fuel up on strong coffee at dawn. It is a place of transit, where the 'dregs' refers affectionately to the bottom of a good cup of coffee or ale, shared among friends.

pointsOfInterest.name: TBD (The Best Drink)
pointsOfInterest.description: Conversation hums over the clink of glasses, carrying the smell of spilled ale and experimental cocktails through a well-used drinking room. Cats slip between chair legs while patrons settle into corners to trade news. Beneath the everyday bustle hangs the watchfulness of an occupied city, where even an ordinary conversation can carry more than one meaning.
pointsOfInterest.summary: The former Cat and Hound, reborn as The Best Drink: a Stomion tavern that serves as the party’s business, gathering place, and base of operations.

properties.Proprietors: The adventuring party; Veylan secured the property deed under a shell identity.
properties.Services: Drinks, cocktails, and a place to gather.
properties.Notable Regular: Lilibeth Goldwyn, who works behind the bar and experiments with cocktails.
properties.Animals: A stray mother cat gave birth to seven kittens here.

detailSections.heading: A Name Worth Keeping
detailSections.body: When reports described the former Cat and Hound’s new name as 'to be determined,' the party adopted TBD as the name itself. Its hidden meaning is The Best Drink. Earlier accounts also call the premises the Black Rose.

detailSections.heading: Behind the Bar
detailSections.body: Lilibeth has worked at the bar and experimented enthusiastically with potential house cocktails. Rain gave shelter to a pregnant stray cat, who delivered seven kittens inside the tavern. The establishment has become a home as well as a business.

detailSections.heading: History
detailSections.body: The Cat and Hound was previously run by the sisters Kallista and Eleni. In its former incarnation, it was a warm, cozy sanctuary on a raised mezzanine overlooking the street, its timbers vibrating with the passing of nearby trains. It was a beloved evening refuge for the city’s mid-level workers. Kallista, a stoic veteran of the national army known as 'The Hound,' handled security and heavy lifting. The name commemorated her lost lover, a Felis—'The Cat'—who vanished during the war. Eleni, who had worked the floor under the previous owner, managed the patrons. The sisters sourced fresh ingredients at dawn and served high-quality, inexpensive meals, with piano music and hearty stew among the tavern’s comforts. Under their management, it opened from 4 PM to midnight and prohibited politics and magic, although the sisters privately sympathized with the rebellion. These hours, prices, and rules describe the former establishment, not confirmed policies under the party’s ownership. An Imperial raid made it part of the party’s earliest struggle in Stomion. Veylan later acquired the seized property through Arfraduren Bank under a shell identity, securing a six-month rent deferral and giving the group a permanent foothold in the city.

detailSections.heading: Behind Closed Doors — GM Information
detailSections.body: The party uses the tavern as a cover business and intelligence hub. Beneath the building lies a concealed cult chamber with connections to deeper tunnels. The premises offer shelter and access to the city’s hidden routes, but official interest in the cellar threatens the security of the entire operation.

pointsOfInterest.name: Govenors Gate
pointsOfInterest.description: Locally reviled as 'The Traitor's Arch,' the Governor's Gate is a structure of ancient, gorgeous Elven stonework that serves as the choke point between the city and the puppet administration on Aelindor's Isle.
pointsOfInterest.summary: An ancient, fortified Elven gatehouse guarding the bridge to Aelindor's Isle, manned by corrupt City Watch and nicknamed 'The Traitor's Arch'.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: The gatehouse consists of two square, crenellated towers flanking a heavy, reinforced arched entry at the end of a long stone causeway. It is not manned by the elite Beccin Black Guard, but by a hand-picked detachment of the City Watch. These guards enforce a strict 'official business only' policy, processing visitors with invasive searches and mandatory escorts—unless, of course, one can pay the steep bribes they are known to accept. In the past, the gate was a gathering point for desperate refugees begging for aid, but the terrifying silhouette of the Beccin airship hovering just above the castle has largely scared them away, leaving the bridge eerily quiet.

pointsOfInterest.name: Governor's Castle
pointsOfInterest.description: Commonly known as the Governor's Castle, this structure is historically Castle Aelindor, an ancient Elven fortress of elegant and sea-facing balconies.
pointsOfInterest.summary: The ancient Elven Castle Aelindor, now the seat of the puppet Magistrate Vael, a collaborator trapped between a hateful populace and the ruthless Beccin Empire.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: It is currently the seat of Magistrate Vael, the nervous and sweating face of the 'Traitor Elf' administration. Clad in an ill-fitting Beccin tunic that symbolizes her uncomfortable submission, Vael stands paralyzed between a populace that loathes her collaboration and an Empire that views her softness as an inefficiency. She rules in name only, reading decrees of quarantine and tax hikes to angry crowds from the safety of the castle walls, while the black shadow of a Beccin airship hovers perpetually overhead. Unknown to her, she is merely a puppet being groomed by Overseer Verrick.

pointsOfInterest.name: Hags Hovel
pointsOfInterest.description: Within the chaotic sprawl of The Shacks lies Hags Hovel, a notorious dive bar built from the rusted hull of a scavenged tugboat that has been aggressively expanded with bolted-on scrap and driftwood.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A seedy tavern in The Shacks built from an expanded tugboat, run by a cantankerous old woman and guarded by a massive Dragonborn, serving as a safe haven for illicit deals.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: The establishment earns its name from its proprietor, an unpleasant and razor-tongued old woman whose eclectic collection of personal trinkets lines the grime-slicked walls. The roof is a sieve of leaks caught by a maze of buckets, and the air is thick with the smell of wet rot and desperation. Imperial patrols avoid the venue entirely, making it a sanctuary for the city's criminal element; while the house doesn't sell contraband, the patrons openly do. A back room hosts high-stakes gambling and hushed contracts, all enforced by 'Kiddo,' a massive Dragonborn bouncer who ensures that the lawlessness remains organized.

pointsOfInterest.description: Formerly known as the Xylokoilo Lyceum (Ancient for 'Woodhollow'), this institution was rebranded to align with the modern sensibilities of the Beccin occupation.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A magic school formerly known as Xylokoilo, where students are strictly trained for military service and failure results in severe cognitive decline.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: It is named after Hera Vlachouli, a figure sympathetic to the Empire, helping to ease the local populace's disdain for the wizarding class that largely fled the country. Led by Headmistress Elpida Tata, who walks a razor-thin line between Imperial loyalty and academic preservation, the Institute focuses on producing magically capable assets for the Beccin military. The curriculum is rigorous, strictly categorized, and heavily monitored; Wild Magic is treated as a dangerous pathology to be suppressed. Students wear robes blending classical Greek drapes with color-coded house linings. Failure is not an option—those who wash out are sent to 'remedial programs' from which they return noticeably simpler and mentally eroded. Beneath the school lies a sealed subterranean complex now known as 'The Deeproot,' rumored to hold secrets from the school's older, wilder days.

pointsOfInterest.description: Rising above the smog of the lower city, Merchant's Hill is the residential enclave of Stomion's 'Old Money.'
pointsOfInterest.summary: Merchant's Hill is an elite residential district for the city's 'Old Money,' characterized by owner-maintained ornate street lamps, polite social exclusion, and the Public Observatory.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: It is a neighborhood of fading but dignified elegance, home to wealthy regional merchants and ancient families who cling to the pre-occupation past. While the residents possess little actual political authority—having been stripped of real power by the Beccin administration—they maintain a stubborn veneer of influence through social exclusion and a culture that is 'snobby, but not overly rude.' The district is visually defined by its unique lighting: rather than uniform municipal posts, the streets are illuminated by ornate, distinct oil lamps. Each lamp is commissioned and zealously maintained by the owner of the nearest manor as a fierce display of status and wealth. The area is not gated but is heavily patrolled by the City Watch, who politely ensure that the uninvited do not linger. Notable residents include Veylan Wollif, the envoy for the Iron Coffer. The district’s crown jewel is the Public Observatory, a place of quiet contemplation where the elite watch the stars, ignoring the industrial smoke rising from the districts below.

pointsOfInterest.description: Suspended between the central spires like a glittering jewel in a stone web, the Oikos Atrium is a colossal, crystalline geodesic dome that houses the last breath of the Old World.
pointsOfInterest.summary: A suspended glass conservatory preserving extinct magical flora, serving as the neutral social hub for the Great Houses' political maneuvering and high-society events.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: It serves as the private botanical conservatory and primary social salon for those in the Synedrion of Blood. Inside, the air is perfumed and perfectly humidified, maintained by complex weather wards that nurture flora extinct everywhere else in Eschatia. Silver-ferns from the Lost Age and glowing moon-blooming lotuses. It is here that 'The Season' takes place: a perpetual cycle of tea ceremonies, marriage negotiations, and high-stakes political maneuvering disguised as leisure. By ancient treaty, no violence is permitted within the glass, making it the only place where rival Great Houses can meet face-to-face to trade secrets.

pointsOfInterest.name: The Shop
pointsOfInterest.description: Welcome to The Shop!
pointsOfInterest.summary: A place of creators and workers.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: Back in the glory days, this facility was a premier, open-floor smithy. Now? It’s a survival rig adapted for the grind. We stripped the layout and partitioned it into flats to house a crew of makers and their families. The main floor got squeezed, but it remains the beating heart of the operation: a high-traffic, communal fabrication zone where every discipline from leather-working to cold forging collides. We keep a resident fabricator on site, bunked in a solo unit. They machine the components, true the grinding wheels, and repair the communal gear. In exchange for keeping the shop running, the rest of the crew knows when to look the other way. If a shipment of non-standard, unregistered materials hits the loading dock? We didn't see a thing. The heat is high, and the quarters are tight. We don't act loud; we just hammer hard.
