regions.name: Academy Gardens
regions.description: Academy Gardens surrounds Hera Vlachouli’s Institute of the Arcane with winding waterways, immaculate lawns, and shaded walking paths. Students practice magic beneath the trees while wealthy residents stroll grounds maintained by unseen servants. Though open to the public, nightly patrols preserve the district’s carefully ordered atmosphere.
regions.summary: A wealthy park district surrounding Hera Vlachouli’s Institute, where manicured gardens, public spellwork, and magical lights create one of Stomion’s most elegant public spaces.

regions.name: Aelindor's Isle
regions.description: Aelindor’s Isle rises from the water in salt-darkened cliffs, weathered rock shelves, and narrow ledges softened by manicured gardens. Ancient Castle Aelindor serves as the seat of state administration, reached through a single heavily guarded bridge, while a black Beccin airship hangs above its Elven spires.
regions.summary: A restricted government island centered on ancient Castle Aelindor, guarded by a fortified bridge and overshadowed by the Beccin occupation.

regions.name: Brighttfyr
regions.description: Brighttfyr occupies Stomion’s rocky downriver point, its salt-streaked stone and bright glass washed by the High Beacon’s immense oil flame. Clerics of Origin and Bethtox divide each day into four watches to keep the light burning, guiding ships through the river mouth while the district hums long after the rest of the city sleeps.
regions.summary: A holy district at the river mouth where priests keep the High Beacon burning through every watch to guide ships into Stomion.

regions.name: Cathedral
regions.description: The Cathedral crowns the highest point on Stomion’s main island, its beautiful sanctuary open to worshippers of many faiths. Priests of the most widely revered gods tend prominent shrines within the main hall, while smaller statues, alcoves, and offerings honor the countless other deities of the pantheons. It is a shared place of prayer rather than the seat of any single faith.
regions.summary: The highest point on Stomion’s main island, crowned by a grand public sanctuary honoring gods from across the pantheons.

regions.name: Coin's Curve
regions.description: Coin’s Curve sits above the sweeping bend of an open rail cut, with stone banks, counting houses, and financial temples lining the streets along its rim. The clatter of trains rises from below—the sound of money, as bankers call it—while private guards in polished plate enforce dress codes and bar anyone without business. After closing, the district empties into silence above vaults rumored to be carved deep into the bedrock.
regions.summary: Stomion’s heavily guarded financial district, where banks and counting houses overlook an open railway and rumored vaults reach deep beneath the streets.

regions.name: Harrowholm
regions.description: Connected to the city by a long, defensible stone bridge, Harrowholm is a small, fortified island that serves as the seat of Stomion’s municipal government. The district is named for 'The Harrowing,' a tragic historical event where the city's ancient noble family sacrificed themselves to seal a gate to the Shadowfell—an act that infused their surviving bloodline with latent sorcerous power. The island is dominated by a distinctive round tower which houses the headquarters of the City Watch on its lower levels, while the upper levels serve as the residence for the current Mayor, Thaddeus Vane, and his family. Mayor Vane is widely regarded as a weak leader who works far too comfortably with the Beccin occupiers, creating a local government that operates autonomously in name only. He rules with a small circle of appointed officials, protected from the tax-paying populace that elected him by the surrounding waters and the City Watch barracks beneath his floorboards. Rumors persist among the guards that the island is haunted by the shadows of the original noble sacrifice, and deep beneath the tower lies a dungeon that holds more than just common criminals.
regions.summary: Harrowholm is the fortified island seat of the City Mayor and City Watch, named for an ancient noble sacrifice that haunts the site.

regions.name: Highhammer
regions.description: A district of imposing stone and polished brass, Highhammer stands as a meticulously curated monument to Dwarven industry and destiny. This area is kept unnervingly clean—a 'model district' designed to showcase the might of the Ossurian Forges to the occupied populace. The skyline is dominated by The High Hammer of Matrix, a temple dedicated to the God of the Forge and Destiny who liberated the dwarves from their ancient oppressor. The temple is marked by a colossal, ornamental hammer suspended above its entrance, a symbol of the destiny forged within. The streets are lined with the high-end showrooms of the Beccin Empire's military industrial complex, displaying gleaning weapons and marvels. While these storefronts are open to the public, the workshops behind them are restricted zones. The district is primarily inhabited by Dwarves—both Ossurian expats and local artisans. It is also the location of the 'Old Furnace.'
regions.summary: Highhammer is a pristine, Dwarf-majority district housing the Temple of Matrix and the showrooms of the Ossurian Forges.

regions.name: Merchant's Hill
regions.description: Merchant’s Hill is Stomion’s old-money residential enclave, preserving the fading elegance of families wealthy before the occupation. Each household commissions the ornate oil lamp nearest its property, turning the streets into a quiet competition of glass, metalwork, and family taste. The district is not formally gated, but City Watch patrols politely ensure that uninvited visitors do not linger.
regions.summary: An old-money residential district of private manors, ornate street lamps, and polite but persistent exclusion.

regions.name: Mirkwater
regions.description: Mirkwater is a dense, practical waterfront where workshops, subdivided flats, handcarts, and small traders compete for every dry patch of street. Places such as the Shop combine housing and fabrication beneath the same roof, with workers sharing heat, tools, and loading space. The district is loud, crowded, and full of people accustomed to repairing what the city cannot afford to replace.
regions.summary: A crowded working waterfront of workshops, cramped housing, and small trade, where Stomion’s makers and off-ledger economy stay in motion.

regions.name: Mirkwwater Landing
regions.description: Mirkwwater Landing is Mirkwater’s direct connection to the water, handling the district’s everyday flow of passengers, supplies, and small cargo. Practical and busy rather than formal, it links the landing traffic with Mirkwater’s workshops, traders, and crowded streets.
regions.summary: A working landing serving Mirkwater, where passengers, materials, and cargo move between the neighborhood and the water.

regions.name: Newkort
regions.description: Newkort is a dense residential district of crowded tenements and narrow single-family dwellings built shoulder to shoulder. Many mid-ranking Beccin and State officials and officers make their homes here, giving the neighborhood a respectable character without the wealth of Stomion’s grander districts. Bakeries and food stalls occupy ground floors and street corners, serving residents from early morning into the evening.
regions.summary: A dense residential district of tenements, narrow family homes, bakeries, and food stalls, favored by mid-ranking Beccin and State officials.

regions.name: Northgate
regions.description: Renamed for its location adjacent to the city's North Gate, this district is a bustling hub of overland travelers. The streets are perpetually active with wagons hauling lumber and fresh produce from the northern fields. It is a welcoming, family-safe neighborhood characterized by practical homes, local bakeries, and taverns that specialize in hearty stews and warm beds for weary road-weary visitors. While a small contingent of Beccin Imperial guards maintains a visible presence at the gate itself, the district's true anchor is the House of the Lost and Wayward. It is a respectable funeral parlor and counseling center staffed by doctor-like professionals and funded by open donations.
regions.summary: Northgate is a busy, family-friendly district defined by overland trade and traveler amenities, funeral parlor, and conselor center.

regions.name: Oldfort
regions.description: As the oldest district in Stomion, Oldfort is a jarring collision of eras. The district centers on the titular 'Old Fort,' a weathered stone structure that once defended the coast but now serves as the weary heart of municipal administration. However, it is the Beccin Embassy that truly dominates the skyline; a massive, modern structure of red brick and glass that has been annexed onto the ancient fort, nearly eclipsing it in size and standing as a physical manifestation of the occupation. During the day, the streets are a chaotic sea of misery and opportunism: long, snaking lines of citizens wait hours to pay the 'Math Tax' or plead for permits, while 'fixers,' scribes, and disbarred lawyers buzz through the crowds selling shortcuts. The air is thick with the smell of ink, despair, and ozone. Yet, the moment the clock strikes 4:30 PM, the district dies instantly. The shutters slam down, the bureaucrats flee, and Oldfort becomes a ghost town of silent stone and ticking clocks.
regions.summary: The historic heart of Stomion, where the ancient city administration building is physically and metaphorically overshadowed by the massive, modern Beccin Embassy, creating a district of bureaucracy.

regions.name: Oldmarket
regions.description: Oldmarket is one of Stomion’s historic trading districts, where goods pass through warehouses before being divided among the city’s smaller markets and shops. The Merchant Senate and Imperial Offices stand among its warehouses and public buildings, placing local commerce and State administration side by side. An old public bath survives among the district’s busier institutions.
regions.summary: Stomion’s historic wholesale market and civic-commercial center, home to the Merchant Senate and Imperial Offices.

regions.name: Roselantern
regions.description: Roselantern is Stomion’s district of nightlife, art, and celebration. Musicians, performers, professional companions, tavernkeepers, and food sellers keep its streets lively after dark. Traditional covered arcades shelter shops, cafés, and small stages, while newer amusement halls offer mechanical games, magical diversions, and contests of skill. Warm colored lanterns illuminate the revelry long after the city’s working districts have closed.
regions.summary: Stomion’s late-night district of music, performance, food, companionship, and arcades both old and new.

regions.name: Saltmarket
regions.description: Saltmarket stretches between Stomion’s two docks as a broad open-air marketplace and public gathering ground. Vendors sell salt, fish, preserved food, and harbor provisions around a central space kept open for civic notices, proclamations, speeches, and other announcements. On busy days, dockworkers, sailors, merchants, and residents turn the district into one of the city’s loudest meeting places.
regions.summary: An open waterfront market stretching between Stomion’s two docks, where daily trade shares space with public announcements and gatherings.

regions.name: Side Harbor
regions.description: Side Harbor is Stomion’s international working harbor, where foreign flags and unfamiliar languages mingle with dock bells, cargo crews, and local traffic. The Imperial Admiralty watches from offices along the waterfront, while foreign concerns such as the Wolgari Trading Company maintain their own docks and houses of trade. Sailors, commercial agents, harbor officials, and laborers keep the quays busy through every arrival and departure.
regions.summary: Stomion’s international working harbor, where foreign crews, trading houses, naval officials, and local dock labor meet.

regions.name: Smartwalk
regions.description: Smartwalk is Stomion’s working civic district, centered on the State Government Building and local administration; no Beccin offices operate here. State clerks, advocates, couriers, and visitors share its streets with magic shops and specialist businesses. Taxis and open buggies wait for fares while communications lines carry a steady stream of official and commercial traffic through the district.
regions.summary: A civic and professional district of State offices, magic shops, hired carriages, and busy communications.

regions.name: Steamwall
regions.description: The Steamwall is a dedicated industrial zone defined not by walls of stone, but by a dense, hissing curtain of vents and pressurized piping. The air here is thick with smog and strange, unnaturally colored chemical vapors that swirl under the light of sickly yellow oil lamps, which burn day and night to cut through the haze. It serves as the component heart of the city's production, churning out gears, rivets, and refined fuel to feed the factories elsewhere. Unlike the state-run facilities, the Steamwall is privately held—the Beccin Empire explicitly owns nothing here, leaving the district in the hands of ruthlessly efficient private consortiums. It is a district of pure utility; the smell of copper and metal hangs heavy, and while the noise of grinding machinery is deafening by day, the area empties completely at night, as no one is willing to live amidst the toxic fumes.
regions.summary: A uninhabited industrial utility district defined by a dense tangle of hissing pipes and chemical vents.

regions.name: The Badges
regions.description: 'The Badges' is the dedicated residential enclave for the city's martial forces, housing both the occupying Beccin troops and the local 'Grey' collaborators. Contrary to the expected segregation, the housing here is of uniformly decent quality for both factions, fostering a sense of unified purpose rather than hierarchy. It is a district of families as much as soldiers, filled with the bustling domestic life of those on the empire's payroll. The streets are washed in the colors of the Empire, draped heavily in flags and patriotic propaganda to keep morale high. The district's most envied features are its exclusive commissaries—well-stocked stores that offer goods and luxuries often unavailable or unaffordable to the general public. Despite its military nature, the district is not a closed fortress; it remains surprisingly open to the city at large, projecting an image of confidence and integration rather than fear.
regions.summary: A surprisingly accessible residential district housing Beccin soldiers, local 'Grey' forces, and their families, defined by high morale, imperial propaganda, and exclusive amenities superior to the rest of the city.

regions.name: The Bulwark
regions.description: The Bulwark is not a single wall, but a layered defensive crossing built across the vast natural chasm separating Aelindor’s Isle from the rest of Stomion. Merchant Gate anchors the cityward approach, while narrow bridges, stone causeways, and reinforced guard stations lead toward Governor’s Gate and the final crossing to the island. Traffic can be stopped at several points long before anyone reaches the governor’s seat.
regions.summary: A fortified sequence of bridges, causeways, gates, and guard stations spanning the vast natural chasm that separates Aelindor’s Isle from Stomion.

regions.name: The Chimes
regions.description: Chimgate is the cultural and commercial zenith of Stomion’s artisan district. Despite the name, no defensive gate stands here; the title is a legacy of the ancient wind chimes that once hung from every eave and archway 'back in the day.' A handful of these original chimes remain, filling the plaza with a soft, melodic background music that encourages hushed tones and polite behavior. This is a district of high-end commerce where the streets are uncrowded and the atmosphere is undeniably snobbish; one does not simply 'shop' at Chimgate, one selects fine jewelry, clothes, and art from masters of the craft. The clientele is a mix of wealthy tourists, established merchants, and high-ranking Beccin occupiers seeking to acquire local luxury. Deals are frequently finalized over delicate infusions at The Azure Teapot, the district's premier tea house.
regions.summary: The legacy-named hub of the high-end artisan district, characterized by soft music from ancient chimes, snobbish exclusivity, and the popular Azure Teapot tea house.

regions.name: The Hallow Heart
regions.description: The Hallow Heart is where the rail lines entering and leaving Stomion converge with the line to the Raildock. Water towers and three great bridges dominate the district, with only a handful of residences standing among the infrastructure. Named for the celebrated inventor Valen Hallow, the junction is vital to both the city’s transportation network and its water supply.
regions.summary: Stomion’s central rail junction and water-tower district, named for the famed local inventor Valen Hallow.

regions.name: The Shacks
regions.description: Description 'The Shacks' is a chaotic, unplanned warren of survival that clings to the edge of the city. True to its name, the district is composed almost entirely of improvised structures built from scavenged scrap metal, driftwood, and stolen industrial refuse. It is the refuge of the city’s poorest citizens, the displaced, and those who operate 'off-ledger' to survive the occupation. In a stark departure from the suffocating surveillance of the city center, Imperial patrols are shockingly rare here, effectively ceding the territory to locals and making it a dangerous but necessary haven for those needing to disappear.
regions.summary: A lawless, sprawling shantytown built from scavenged scrap on the city's fringe, inhabited by the desperate and those living 'off-ledger' largely ignored by Imperial patrols.

regions.name: The Swath
regions.description: The Swath is Stomion at its most hard-scrabble: dense, worn down, and constantly shaken by nearby rail traffic. Workers, families, and the city’s poorest residents crowd into buildings repeatedly divided, repaired, and repurposed, while taverns and food sellers offer affordable comfort between shifts. Freight, soot, and vibration from the Raildock shape the district’s daily rhythm.
regions.summary: A hard-scrabble rail-side district of crowded housing, labor yards, inexpensive taverns, and Stomion’s poorest residents.

regions.name: The Towers
regions.description: Rising high above the smog of Stomion, 'The Towers' serves as the exclusive, vertical enclave of the city's sorcerous elite. It is a district of soaring stone spires connected by elegant sky-bridges, allowing residents to traverse the area without ever touching the ground level. The atmosphere is distinct from the rest of the city; bathed in the cold, steady glow of blue-white magical arc lamps, it stands in sharp contrast to the flickering yellow gaslights of the Beccin occupation. Access is strictly controlled through a combination of physical checkpoints and magical ward-alarms that alert private security to unauthorized entrants; those caught without proper paperwork are stripped of their possessions and ejected. Inside, the Beccin presence is almost non-existent, leaving the powerful Great Houses to plot, dine in high-end bakeries, and flaunt the latest fashions in relative sovereignty. While the spires represent the height of luxury, the foundations are rumored to be honeycombed with ancient crypts holding the secrets—and remains—of a first sorcerers.
regions.summary: An elite, restricted district of soaring spires and sky-bridges inhabited by sorcerers, lit by magical arc lamps and rumored to sit atop ancient crypts.

regions.name: Wallside
regions.description: Wallside is a small residential district built along Stomion’s outer wall. Its closely packed homes belong largely to working households with steady but limited incomes. Neither prosperous nor destitute, the neighborhood is defined by practical housing, careful maintenance, and families making the most of what they have.
regions.summary: A small lower-middle-class residential district of modest, closely packed homes along Stomion’s outer wall.

main_continent.name: Fair

regions.name: Aethelumbra
regions.description: The ancient Aethelumbra, know as the home of the Iron Mountain Dwarves, have carved their kingdom into vast, honeycomb cities within the mountains, a realm governed by a monarch and a unique two-house parliament of commoners and guild masters. Their industrious society is deeply private, shaped by bitter experience with outsiders. They hold a weary suspicion of the elves since an incident involving a destroyed caffeine-fungus, but this pales before their outright hatred for the Athenaeum, who once turned the dwarven lands into a battleground for a human war the dwarves neither wanted nor cared for.
regions.summary: The reclusive Iron Mountain Dwarves carve honeycomb cities deep within the mountains, harboring a bitter hatred for outsiders.

regions.name: Albynor
regions.description: Albynor is a realm ruled by clans, a people as stern and unyielding as the mountains and hills they inhabit. They are masters of stone and steel, their honor bound by oaths as old as the Highlands themselves.
regions.summary: In this stern realm, mountain clans rule with honor bound by oaths as old as the Highlands themselves.

regions.name: Arfordir
regions.description: Famed for its fertile valleys and fragrant lavender fields, this kingdom is breathing a collective sigh of relief. It has only recently cast down a usurper to welcome its rightful Queen Eloise I, and a sense of hard-won peace now settles over the land.
regions.summary: This kingdom of fertile valleys and fragrant fields now enjoys a hard-won peace under its restored queen.

regions.name: Athenaeum
regions.description: Born from the hubris of post-war treaties, this league of city-states is ruled from the sacred lake where the God of Magic died. A tense quiet now hangs over its marble halls after a shadowy cataclysm nearly tore the capital apart, leaving the nation's fate in the hands of a single, powerful archivist.
regions.summary: A league of city-states reels in tense quiet after a magical cataclysm nearly tore its capital apart.

regions.name: Bec
regions.description: Bec is the glittering, autocratic heart of the ascendant Beccin Empire, a vast land stretching from the sun-drenched rice paddies of its southern provinces to the frigid, windswept mountains of the north. Its society is one of stark contrasts, where the unimaginable opulence of the nobility's gilded palaces is built upon the endless toil of the peasantry. Fueled by relentless expansion and the flow of tribute from its satellite states, the empire's wealth and power grow with each passing year.
regions.summary: The glittering heart of an ascendant empire, Bec's opulence is built on the toil of its peasantry.

regions.name: Blū
regions.description: A nation of humming factory-cities and alchemical ingenuity, where every citizen is a vital cog in a grand, well-oiled machine. Generations of gnomish innovation have forged a society of relentless progress and unparalleled collective welfare, making the state itself their greatest invention.
regions.summary: Generations of gnomish ingenuity have forged a nation of humming factory-cities and relentless progress.

regions.name: Bugon Kingdom
regions.description: Often Called "Bugdom" for the fact when people first found the people of this island they were dealing with a bad case of sea spiders.
regions.summary: This island kingdom earned its nickname 'Bugdom' after outsiders discovered them during a sea spider infestation.

regions.name: Confederacy of Half Hieghts
regions.description: The Confederacy of Half Heights is a vibrant constitutional commonwealth governed by a Chancellor. The region is defined by its dramatic, sweeping canyons, which are naturally formed, though local folklore insists they were carved from the earth by ancient giants. Enjoying a balmy, Mediterranean climate, the landscape is dotted with fragrant shrubs of summer jasmine and bay laurel. To thrive in this environment, the inhabitants have mastered elaborate rain collection systems to sustain their terraced gardens and daily needs. Though the region earned its name as the ancestral homeland of the halflings, the Confederacy is now a welcoming melting pot of diverse races. Their settlements are a marvel of engineering, beautifully blending the colorful, sun-drenched masonry of Anzio-style villas with the practical, cliff-integrated tiers of Pueblo architecture. Navigating the steep canyon trails are large, flightless avians that the locals use as beasts of burden instead of traditional horses. Despite the peaceful and bustling nature of these communities, the region still holds ancient secrets, with forgotten tombs hidden deep within the shadowy recesses of the mountains and canyon floors.
regions.summary: This territory is a peaceful alliance of communities nestled among tranquil canyons and valleys.

regions.name: Cursed Oldlin
regions.description: This land was once a sun-kissed jewel, a vibrant valley whose people knew only bountiful harvests and bright horizons. That was before the arrival of him, Strahd. He took the valley first by the niceness think himself freed from damnation, then the cycle started a new and his dark pact poisoned the very soil, bleeding the life and color from the world. Now the land is a twisted reflection of its master's tormented soul: the sun is a stranger, the forests have grown teeth, and the entire valley is caged in a ghostly mist—a monument not to a kingdom, but to one man's tragic and eternal damnation.
regions.summary: Once a vibrant valley, this land is now a twisted reflection of its master's eternal damnation, caged in mist.

regions.name: Farnear
regions.description: While the farming communities of the great river basin are as old as any on the continent, the nation of Farnear is a recent invention. For generations, this fertile breadbasket was a disconnected patchwork of independent nations. This changed when the pragmatic gnomes of Blū, seeking a more efficient and stable trading partner, brokered a grand unification - this caused a short and violent civil war. By offering infrastructure investments and access to advanced technology, they helped organize them into a cohesive republic. The name 'Farnear' was chosen by the new council to signify their new reality: no longer a 'far'-flung collection of nations, but a single, 'near' neighbor, united in prosperity.
regions.summary: Gnomish pragmatism helped forge a patchwork of farming communities into a single, prosperous republic.

regions.name: Ferendel
regions.description: Nestled within a dramatic fjord, this kingdom was for a generation shrouded in a mysterious, self-imposed isolation. Today, its bustling port has reopened to the world, yet the nation retains an atmosphere of guarded secrets and quiet resilience.
regions.summary: A fjord kingdom reopens its ports to the world after a generation of mysterious, self-imposed isolation.

regions.name: Goldwind
regions.description: In this sun-scorched expanse, where glittering sands whisper tales of easily won fortunes and powerful dust devils carve canyons, a rough-and-tumble society thrives. Here, beneath the vast, unforgiving sky, disputes are settled with a blend of frontier justice and arcane arts.
regions.summary: In this sun-scorched frontier, a rough society thrives where fortunes are won with raw justice and arcane arts.

regions.name: Harold Ford
regions.description: An ancient kingdom forged from the union of proud and culturally distinct peoples, its rolling green hills and rugged highlands are often shrouded in mist. From the sprawling, historic capital that shares the nation's name, a single crown now governs the formerly warring lands, navigating a delicate peace built on a shared, yet often contested, history.
regions.summary: From its mist-shrouded capital, an ancient kingdom navigates a delicate peace between formerly warring peoples.

regions.name: Himmelsrand
regions.description: Himmelsrand is a realm where the earth rises violently to meet the heavens, a jagged expanse of gray stone and white silence. To travel here is to breathe air so cold it tastes like iron, walking beneath pine forests so ancient and dense that they swallow the light of the pale sun. The province is defined by its verticality; massive, cloud-piercing peaks ring the horizon like the walls of a fortress, their summits forever shrouded in violent blizzards, while the valleys below are carpeted in golden tundra grass and winding, icy rivers that freeze solid in the depths of winter. The land feels lived-in but wild, marked by the decaying grandeur of the Zarate of Tiamat. You cannot walk the mountain passes without seeing the scars of that lost - pillars jutting from the mountainsides like broken ribs, or the crumbling foundations of black citadels now reclaimed by moss and heavy drifts of snow. These ruins are no longer seats of power, but simply part of the geography, looming silently over the wooden villages of the Nords. At night, when the auroras bleed emerald and violet across the sky, the wind howls through the hollow arches of Tiamat’s fallen monuments, creating a mournful song that reminds every traveler that this savage beauty was once tamed by something far darker.
regions.summary: Himmelsrand is a savage northern wilderness, once the imperial seat of the Zarate of Tiamat, reminders of a dark power now reclaimed by the ice.

regions.name: Icebeach
regions.description: This brutal, frozen frontier is a land of hardy survivors and terrifying beasts, where scattered settlements cling to life like flickering candles against an oppressive and isolating terrain. Legends of a lich's forgotten fortress and secrets buried within the great glacier's sunless heart lend a palpable sense of terror to the landscape.
regions.summary: This brutal, frozen frontier is a land of hardy survivors, terrifying beasts, and legends of a lich's fortress.

regions.name: Iron Bash
regions.description: Life on the islands of the Iron Bash is tethered to the tides of the immortal Empress Mael Muire. Her people enjoy a profound security; the Empress's will is the sea itself, forming a protective wall of storms and treacherous currents that no foreign navy dares to cross. She is their guardian and their sustainer, calming the waters for their fishing fleets and trade. Yet, the sea is also their greatest fear. Her sanity is a fickle ocean, and a sudden, deep swell of madness can turn a minor offense into a capital crime. This unleashes the terrifying wrath that gives the nation its name: the 'Bash' is the sound of a tidal wave of her own making, crashing against the cliffs with the force of hammered iron. The people of the Iron Bash offer their Empress both genuine gratitude and cautious obedience, forever reading the moods of the ocean for a sign of the storm within their queen.
regions.summary: The people here live in cautious obedience to their immortal Empress, whose control of the sea offers both protection and terror.

regions.name: Kargotha
regions.description: The full name is the Kargotha - The Ormakth Hegemony of the Kaliean Reach.  This land is not a nation but an area under the control of a warlord raiding party of goliaths.  They are a bunch of clans all ran by members of the Ormakth, said to be a line similar to the one that Beckarak forged.
regions.summary: This territory is not a nation but the raiding grounds of the Ormakth Hegemony, a powerful goliath alliance.

regions.name: Nokkar the Nag
regions.description: Originally charted as 'The Rest' due to its proximity to a fabled dark fortress on the coast of Icebeach, this remote, ice-bound island has a history steeped in superstition and linguistic corruption. Dwarven mariners, finding the name too serene for such a malevolent place, dubbed it 'Nagargrom' ('spirit-stone' in their tongue). This harsh name was eventually clipped and hardened by human sailors into 'Nokkar.' Over generations, its reputation as a perilous and unavoidable navigational hazard earned it the additional moniker 'the Nag.' Legends persist that the island is not merely a landmark but a source of unnatural cold, a place where compasses fail and ghostly lights dance on its frozen peaks, leading many to believe it is a magical prison or the very anchor of some terrible, undying soul to the mortal plane.
regions.summary: Nokkar the Nag is a cursed, frozen island rumored to be a magical prison that disrupts compasses with its unnatural cold.

regions.name: Oldlin
regions.description: Oldlin is less a nation and more a divine sanctuary, a swath of tranquil farmland held sacred by the god Pythia. It is a sparsely populated land of rolling hills and unnaturally bountiful fields, forbidden to outsiders by divine decree. The borders are not guarded by soldiers, but by a palpable aura of judgment, and tales of those who trespassed and vanished are told as warnings in the neighboring realms. Only those who have received 'permission'—a blessing said to be granted through cryptic visions to the worthy or the truly desperate—may enter its serene landscape without incurring the god's wrath.
regions.summary: A divine sanctuary of unnaturally bountiful fields, this tranquil land is forbidden to all but the worthy.

regions.name: Peris Dynasty
regions.summary: The secluded Peris Dynasty governs a remote island whose traditions are known only to its people.

regions.name: Pyralis
regions.description: Sequestered from the world, Pyralis is a monastic society dedicated to a single purpose: watching the heavens. Warmed by the celestial fragment they call the Firesoul, the scholar-monks of Pyralis spend their lives charting cosmic movements and guarding the secrets of their orders. They are a reclusive people, rarely venturing out, but their eerily accurate prophecies—cautiously traded for rare books and knowledge—grant them a quiet influence that belies their profound isolation.
regions.summary: An isolated monastic society charts the cosmos, trading eerily accurate prophecies for rare knowledge.

regions.name: RosWin
regions.description: While newer nations practice agriculture on an industrial scale, the ancient kingdom of RosWin is the continent's traditional, gourmet heartland. Its name is believed to be a corruption of an old phrase for 'Red Wine,' hinting at the rolling, sun-drenched hills of vineyards that define its landscape. Here, heritage and quality are valued over mere quantity; power lies not in armies, but in the unique terroir of the soil and the prestige of a family's ancient vintage. Governed by noble houses whose passionate rivalries over their harvests are legendary, RosWin has long survived as a political crossroads, a neutral ground where treaties are often sealed over a bottle of its finest wine.
regions.summary: In this ancient kingdom, power lies not in armies but in the prestige of a family's sun-drenched vineyards.

regions.name: Seaslinate Dynasty
regions.summary: The Seaslinate Dynasty governs a vibrant chain of tropical islands with a culture tied to the sea.

regions.name: Tewhal
regions.description: A land that was under the control of the gnomes and wizards of the Athenaeum for manufacturing of the flying islands and other machines of war.  It is sparcerly populated now and the land is stained with the remnates of machines of war.  Some ranching farms and towns are up in the high, dry, and desolet dessert.
regions.summary: A desolate wasteland stained with war machines, this land is a shadow of its former life as a gnomish factory zone.

regions.name: The Ashen Lands - Egna
regions.description: Egna, the Ashen Lands, is not a land but a gaping wound upon the world. A great, bleeding artery of magma flows from its shattered core, carving a path through a landscape of splintered basalt and razor-sharp obsidian. Constant ashfall from its countless vents chokes the sky, blanketing the scarred terrain in a perpetual grey twilight. The air is a toxic brew of sulfur and heat, and the ground trembles with the death throes of a land that has torn itself apart, a desolate and broken remnant of a forgotten cataclysm utterly hostile to life.
regions.summary: The Ashen Lands of Egna are the broken, uninhabitable remnants of a great cataclysm, a scarred island perpetually bleeding lava from its fractured heart.

regions.name: The Bulwark Command
regions.description: Officially, The Bulwark Command is a fortified military zone protecting the Beccin Empire's frontier. In truth, it is the empire's most brutal and profitable resource-extraction colony. The landscape is not one of natural beauty, but of colossal quarries and smoke-belching refineries that scar the earth. Under the watchful eyes of imperial legions, a populace of convicts, debtors, and conscripts toils to strip the land of its rare minerals. The entire operation is the personal fiefdom of the Emperor's apprentice Legate Crassus, a notoriously avaricious governor who measures the value of a mountain in ore and the value of a person in the labor they can provide to the imperial coffers.
regions.summary: This fortified military zone is secretly the empire's most brutal and profitable resource-extraction colony.

regions.name: The Counties State of Fair
regions.summary: This peaceful republic is composed of allied counties known for their rich farmland and rolling hills.

regions.name: The Grate Basin
regions.description: Breathtaking and expansive, the deep canyon the stape of the desert. This canyon system vast and dangious, lots of hidden side passages and and uncharted areas.  Only the bravest prospectors or adventures would venture into its sun-scorched depths.
regions.summary: This breathtaking and expansive canyon system is a dangerous labyrinth of hidden, sun-scorched passages

regions.name: The Iron Duchy of Vardenheim
regions.description: To the outside world, the Iron Duchy of Vardenheim is a loyal Beccin vassal state, a windswept land of hardy folk on the imperial frontier, dutifully providing iron and soldiers. This official narrative is a carefully crafted lie. In truth, Vardenheim is the Empire's clandestine operations hub for the entire region. From its grim citadels, the Duke orchestrates a vast network of spies, while its remote location makes it the perfect site for the Empire's most secret and forbidden magical research. It is a paranoid land of watchful eyes, where the wind across the steppes carries whispers of the dark work being done for the glory of the empire.
regions.summary: Appearing as a loyal vassal, this duchy is secretly the empire's hub for spies and forbidden magic.

regions.name: The Kamensky Coast
regions.description: A stark, coastal land wind-carved rock and thin, stubborn soil. Known for its rich marble quarries and strategic ports, the land is sparsely populated. It is a rugged, resource-focused territory, defined more by its harsh geography than by its people.
regions.summary: A rugged territory of hardy folk, the coast is defined by its strategic ports and rich marble quarries.

regions.name: The Kingdom of the Auroran Dwarves
regions.description: This dwarf kingdom is very isolationist, not outright xenophobic but prides themselves in being independet and not involved in geopolitcs.
regions.summary: The isolationist Auroran Dwarves pride themselves on self-sufficiency, remaining apart from global politics.

regions.name: The Krasnogory Krai
regions.description: Governed by a volatile council of jealous Boyars and grizzled Atamans, the people of the Krai are defined by stoykost', a grim fortitude that allows them to endure the unforgiving land and their own leaders' endless feuds. This fragile unity is forged in a shared reverence for the sacred, warmth-giving Solntsekamen they carve from the heart of their mountains, a resource that is both the source of their wealth and the cause of their eternal conflict.
regions.summary: A volatile council of feuding leaders finds fragile unity in their shared reverence for sacred, warmth-giving stones.

regions.name: The Last Elven State
regions.description: As the oldest continuous government on the continent, this ancient and verdant elven democratic republic is a land of deep history and living memory. Though it thrives, its splendor is shadowed by its status as a satellite state, a beautiful but captive jewel in the Beccin Empire's imperial crown.
regions.summary: As the continent's oldest government, this elven republic is now a beautiful but captive jewel in an empire's crown.

regions.name: The Ossurian Forges of Dûr-Gromthal
regions.description: The Ossurian Forges of Dûr-Gromthal is a formidable, soot-stained dwarven kingdom where the roar of industry has violently supplanted the quiet wisdom of ancestors. Once an Ossuary Kingdom guided by an Undying Council, this ancient leadership was overthrown by the revolutionary Anvilwrights, a faction of smiths and engineers who chose survival over tradition during the last great war. Their coup was sealed by the Hearth-Anvil Compact and a pragmatic, secret pact with the Beccin Empire, trading their industrial might for military protection. Today, Dûr-Gromthal is a relentless meritocracy run by the Forgemasters Guild, serving as the official arsenal of the Empire, and its rune-etched hallmark is a symbol of both imperial power and oppression. This alliance has brought them wealth but also the enmity of rivals like the Iron Duchy and the scorn of traditional dwarves, all while the Guild secretly labors to forge its ultimate weapon: an undying army of clockwork soldiers.
regions.summary: The Ossurian Forges of Dûr-Gromthal is an industrial dwarven meritocracy that betrayed its ancestral past to become the powerful, and widely despised, arsenal of the Beccin Empire.

regions.name: The Rimewaste
regions.description: The Rimewastes are less a nation and more a vast, primal expanse of unending ice and wind-scoured rock where civilization holds no sway. Here, nomadic tribes of humans and goliaths follow the migratory paths of colossal megafauna, living not by the laws of kings but by ancient pacts. Survival is the only creed in this land that does not bow to any empire, and the scattered campfires of its people are but fleeting sparks of warmth against a truly unforgiving lands.
regions.summary: In this primal expanse of ice, nomadic tribes hunt colossal megafauna, bowing to no king or empire.

regions.name: The Sea of Silver Tears
regions.summary: A notoriously treacherous sea, its waters are known for unpredictable currents and the ghostly shipwrecks below.

regions.name: The Southern State of Fair
regions.description: Sprawling across the continent's heartland, this vast republic stands as a monument to unity and a crossroads for all peoples. Once a collection of disparate territories, it is now the humming epicenter of culture and governance, where the continent's future is forged in the grand theater of its politics.
regions.summary: This vast republic is the continent's humming epicenter of culture and governance.

regions.name: The Sundered March
regions.description: A volatile, magically-scarred DMZ created by a cataclysmic event at the end of the last great war between the Athenaeum and the Beccin Empire. This wasteland is saturated with raw, unstable arcane energy that makes spellcasting wildly unpredictable and dangerous. The entire region is crisscrossed by immense, permanent wards—lingering echoes of the conflict—that are powerful enough to disintegrate armies, effectively creating an impassable buffer zone. Watched warily by its neighbors, the March serves as a grim and effective deterrent against any large-scale invasion.
regions.summary: A magically-scarred wasteland, the March serves as a grim and impassable buffer zone between empires.

regions.name: The Thane's Steps
regions.description: The Thane's Steps are a rugged chain of wind-scoured islands, named for the legendary Dwarven Thane, Borin Stone-Tread, who was the first to dare the crossing from the mountainous southern mainland to the frozen continent of the north. Each island is considered a footprint on his monumental journey, and the character of the isles changes drastically from south to north, marking the progress of his legendary expedition. The southernmost islands, often called the 'Hearth-Stones,' are heavily fortified extensions of the dwarven homeland. Carved from sea-granite and ancient basalt, their shores are dotted with fortress-lighthouses and deep, protected harbors. Here, hardy dwarven clans mine rare oceanic minerals, fish the rich waters, and maintain the garrisons that protect the vital trade route. The air is cold and misty, but the islands are green with tough, wiry grasses and mosses clinging to the rocks. As one travels north, the islands become smaller, more treacherous, and less hospitable. This central stretch is known as 'The Gamble,' where the Thane's path was most uncertain. The islands here are jagged teeth of black rock, often shrouded in a permanent, disorienting fog. Safe anchorages are few, and the waters are plagued by unpredictable currents and submerged rocks. These islands are largely uninhabited, save for hardy seabirds and lone prospectors seeking their fortune in solitude. The final islands before the northern coast are the 'Rime-Stones.' They are bleak, barren, and perpetually cold, offering the first taste of the arctic winds that howl down from the continent. Snow clings to their peaks year-round, and the sparse vegetation is little more than pale lichen on frost-shattered rock. These are grim outposts, home to a few hardy northern folk, exiled dwarves, or those who hunt the strange, cold-water beasts that swim in the icy depths. They are the last, desperate step before the endless ice.
regions.summary: The Thane's Steps are a perilous chain of islands forged from the warmth of a dwarf homeland to the unforgiving ice of the northern frontier.

regions.name: The Volgrad March
regions.description: A subjugated territory of the Beccin Empire, once home to proud, nomadic horse-clans. Conquered a generation ago to secure a strategic land route for the Empire, the Volg people have been forced from their traditional lifestyle into agricultural servitude. Though imperial fortresses now scar the windswept plains, the occupation is met with simmering resentment and frequent guerilla raids by rebels known as 'land-partisans.' The spirit of the Volg remains unbroken as they fight to reclaim the freedom symbolized by the wild dragons of the nearby Gorá-Sirotá mountain.
regions.summary: In this subjugated land, rebellious horse-clans fight to reclaim their freedom from imperial conquerors.

regions.name: Toppicaea Dynasty
regions.summary: The Toppicaea Dynasty governs from a jewel-like city atop a high plateau, isolated by cliffs.

regions.name: Zafra
regions.description: Known as the Scorched Jewel of the Beccin Empire, the coastal nation of Zafra is a land of simmering resentment. Once a proud maritime kingdom whose fleets ruled the eastern seas, its skilled sailors now serve imperial masters. Beneath the veneer of imperial order, however, the old ways persist in port towns and hidden coves, where smugglers plot and the spirit of piracy waits for the tide to turn against their conquerors.
regions.summary: In this vassal state, the piratical spirit of a conquered maritime kingdom plots against its imperial masters.

main_continent.blurb: From the gold-laced dust of its western canyons to the haunted glaciers of the far north, Fair is a land of adventure and antiquity. Chart a course through newly-opened fjord kingdoms, navigate the politics of ancient empires, and unearth the secrets of a world shaped by heroes and forgotten evils.
main_continent.selectorDescription: The world of Fair, from western canyons to haunted northern ice.

pointsOfInterest.name: Apsley
pointsOfInterest.description: Apsley is the principal city and political heart of the Commonwealth of Half Height, rising in bright tiers of stone, stucco, and retaining walls from its busy docks to its sunlit upper terraces. Long admired as a free-port miracle, the city is known for its ministries, merchant houses, embassies, legal arcades, and the great gondola-funicular spine that binds its heights together. Yet Apsley’s prosperity rests upon a deep social divide: the upper wards enjoy ceremony, comfort, and influence, while the lower districts bear the burdens of freight, customs, industry, and unrest. Its culture is shaped by halfling household politics, public hospitality, and reputation-driven commerce, giving the city a reputation for both generosity and quiet coercion. To admirers, Apsley is proof that disciplined law and trade can secure independence in a dangerous world; to critics, it is a city of polished facades sustained by patronage, inequality, and carefully managed disorder.
pointsOfInterest.summary: Apsley is the cliffside capital of the Commonwealth of Half Height, famed for its trade, wealth, and white-stone terraces.

detailSections.heading: At a glance
detailSections.body: Apsley rises in bright terraces from its harbor, with civic offices, embassies, and merchant houses stacked above the docks.

detailSections.heading: Current tensions
detailSections.body: Its prosperity depends on a managed divide between ceremonial upper wards and freight-heavy lower districts where customs work, industry, and unrest concentrate.

pointsOfInterest.name: Argyra
pointsOfInterest.description: A city of breathtaking, ancient silver spires wrapped in a permanent gray fog (industrial smog mixed with coastal mist).
pointsOfInterest.summary: A city of breathtaking, ancient silver spires wrapped in a permanent gray fog (industrial smog mixed with coastal mist).

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: It is terrifyingly quiet. The Elven Senate debates for months while the city starves under a literal 'Glass Ceiling' built by the Empire. Oppressive silence, beautiful architecture decaying, surveillance state.

pointsOfInterest.name: Castgate
pointsOfInterest.description: Encased within a dome that holds the winter at bay, Castgate's picturesque beauty was earned through legendary battles against a goddess and an undead horde. Today, its bustling streets shine as a beacon of defiant prosperity, a testament to the heroes of Sub Rosa who fought to give the city a future.
pointsOfInterest.summary: This city thrives inside a winter-defying dome, a beacon of prosperity won in legendary battles.

detailSections.heading: Legacy
detailSections.body: Castgate's present prosperity is inseparable from the battles that preserved the city against divine winter and undead siege.

pointsOfInterest.name: Delphi
pointsOfInterest.description: The marble metropolis of Delphi, a jewel on the shore of a sacred lake, is still reeling from the 'Slip'—a magical cataclysm that recently tore through its heart. Now, the air is thick not only with the dust of reconstruction, but with the renewed, ruthless ambitions of its magical elite.
pointsOfInterest.summary: Following a magical cataclysm, the marble city of Delphi rebuilds, fueled by ruthless ambition.

properties.Known for: Marble academies, sacred lake, magical politics

detailSections.heading: After the Slip
detailSections.body: Reconstruction has become a political weapon as Delphi's magical elite compete to shape what rises from the damaged districts.

detailSections.heading: Atmosphere
detailSections.body: Dust, lake mist, and ambition hang over a city trying to look eternal while its foundations are still unsettled.

pointsOfInterest.summary: Once a single hub, these recently divided twin cities now exist as wary, competing city-states.

detailSections.heading: Context

pointsOfInterest.name: Gorá-Sirotá
pointsOfInterest.description: Gorá-Sirotá, the Orphan Mountain, rises in stark isolation from the plains, a peak where dragons are often seen locked in vicious combat.
pointsOfInterest.summary: Atop this lone mountain, dragons viciously battle for the right to claim it as their final roost.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: Common legend holds that they fight over the lost treasure of a dwarven kingdom that was long ago driven from the mountain. The other ledgeons are more primal: the mountain is an ancient and sacred draconic graveyard. The dwarves were not destroyed for their gold, but for the sacrilege of disturbing the hallowed bones within. The dragons of today continue their war not just for treasure, but for the instinctual right to claim the mountain as their final roost.

pointsOfInterest.name: Harold-Ford
pointsOfInterest.description: The sprawling capital of Harold-Ford, which once united warring peoples, stands shrouded in both river mist and a fanatical devotion to its grand temples.
pointsOfInterest.summary: The sprawling capital navigates a tense cold war with a rival empire.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: While the crown maintains a delicate peace over its contested history, the city's avenues are rife with tension fueled by a cold war with a rival empire.

pointsOfInterest.name: Katia
pointsOfInterest.description: Once a serene elven town nestled in an ancient forest at a river's mouth, Katia is now a stark symbol of imperial occupation.
pointsOfInterest.summary: Once a serene elven town, Katia is now a stark symbol of occupation with its ancient forest clear-cut.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: The old woods have been clear-cut for Beccin military operations, leaving the town simmering with quiet resentment under the watch of its unwelcome garrisons.

detailSections.heading: Context

pointsOfInterest.description: Nestled at the head of a deep, fjord, the kingdom's capital rises in a vibrant cascade of color against the stark green and grey of the surrounding cliffs.
pointsOfInterest.summary: This vibrant capital rises in a cascade of colorful buildings against the stark cliffs of its fjord.

detailSections.heading: Context
detailSections.body: Steeply pitched roofs of slate and painted timber in hues of deep crimson, rich ochre, and forest green line the bustling cobblestone streets, which all spiral down to a crescent-shaped harbor alive with the masts of merchant ships and fishing vessels. Presiding over it all from a high, stony bluff is the royal castle, its elegant spires and soaring towers a constant, graceful symbol of the kingdom's enduring prosperity.
